title: Analytics event totals for one session match the rules exactly
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a dispatcher whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > on the Work Orders card, View and Create & Edit are both ticked. The Admin role has both).
  2. In the top bar, choose the location you test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  3. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (the display switcher only shows at 1024 px and wider).
  4. You can open Google Analytics for the property the QA build reports to, at Admin > DebugView. The QA build runs analytics in debug mode, so each event appears in DebugView within a few seconds under your user. If you cannot open DebugView, the event checks in this case cannot be done by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  5. Event names to look for in DebugView: work_orders_display_view (a display was shown), work_orders_field_load and work_orders_density_load (the fields and density you have, once per display per session), work_orders_field_toggle and work_orders_density_change (a saved change).
  6. Your saved display is List and your density has never been changed.
  7. Start a fresh analytics session: close every browser window, open a new private window and sign in.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders (List).
  2. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (the design tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (the design tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (the design tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  5. In Board View's Fields to display (switch to Board View first), turn on Service advisor, Line count and Created date quickly, one after another.
  6. Pick Compact density.
  7. Scroll a long column so more cards load.
  8. In DebugView, count each event name for this session.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • work_orders_display_view = 5 (load 1 + Tech View 1 + Board View 1 + Tech View 1 + Board View again in step 5, 1).
  • work_orders_field_load = 13 + 15 = 28 (Board View and Tech View once each, never again in the session).
  • work_orders_density_load = 2 (once for each of the two displays).
  • work_orders_field_toggle = 3 (one per changed field, even when changed quickly together).
  • work_orders_density_change = 1. Step 7 adds nothing.
  • Grand total = 5 + 28 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 39 events. Use these counts as the sample for the report check in the field selection rate case.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10593 (Story 12, Google Analytics for display and field usage); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S12-E2, S12-R1, S12-R2, S12-R3, S12-R8, read 8 Oct 2026. Event names and timing: SV-10593 comments by Slavcho Mitrov and Milos Vasic, 6 Oct 2026 (the agreed GA4 event table); earlier event contract on Review Decisions page 853901313 (29 Sep 2026) uses older names. Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 10 tests.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-E2: “Verify event multiplicity and sample reporting calculations.”
  • S12-R1: “Measure display usage after successful initial loading and each display or filter-view switch.”
  • S12-R2: “Measure selected and unselected fields available to each user, including untouched defaults and restored preferences. Record this snapshot once per display per session, the first time the user opens that display in the session, not on every open. Field changes are still recorded each time they are saved (S12-R3).”
  • Tech plan Phase 10 tests toggles: “three toggles in one debounce give three events and one PUT”
